A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe the same LongGen study. Text, equations, figures and tables, including image-based tables, support reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4 report original benchmark evaluations, training and inference efficiency measurements, and layer ablations in Tables 2–6 and Figure 2.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including LongGen benchmark accuracies, efficiency measurements and layer ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same hybrid architecture, middle full-attention layers, attention-sink and block-sparse variants, training objective and kernel procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions train on SlimPajama and evaluate NIAH, the first five BABILong tasks, two RULER QA subtasks, MMLU, Math and BBH. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Tables 2–3 retain Attention Sink, H2O, RazorAttention, PyramidKV, sliding window and YOCO, while Tables 3–4 retain the corresponding full-attention comparisons. Figure 3 also retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the reported Llama-2 7B/70B configurations, 5B-token training budget, context-length ranges, accuracy metrics, KV-budget matching and efficiency benchmarking procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Tables 5–6 retain identical ablations of full-attention layer placement and counts. The KV-reduction failure analysis in Section 2 and Figure 3 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the three-seed BABILong sample-generation description, averaging practices and discussion of RULER variability across seeds. No confidence intervals, significance tests or additional repeated-run information appear.

E6.justification: All reported results in Tables 2–6 and Figures 2–3 are unchanged. For example, both LongGen variants retain 100% NIAH pass rates, and Table 4 retains LongGen RULER accuracies of 0.38 and 0.65 for 7B and 70B, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 and Table 1 retain the same complexity expressions, sparse-context assumptions and full/sparse-layer ratio argument. No mathematical definition, derivation or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about integrating context extension with sparse attention, preserving long-context capability and improving efficiency, including 1.55x training speedup and 62% KV-cache reduction.

C2.justification: The explanations for KV-eviction failures, interpretations of layer placement and model scale, and qualifications about underperforming full attention on harder reasoning tasks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 3.2, 4.1 and 4.3 retain the same implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter, hardware and timing details, including block sizes, RoPE settings and the vLLM benchmarking reference. No access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to sparse transformers, state-space models, hybrid architectures and KV-cache eviction methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds equal-contribution asterisks for Suyu Ge, Xihui Lin and Yunan Zhang and the corresponding footnote, and updates the version/date stamp. The scientific prose, terminology and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote and spacing adjustments cause modest text reflow and shifts in section starts and figure placement. All three figures and six tables retain their content, captions and display structure.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies equal authorship and slightly changes layout, while retaining the same scientific text, results, analysis and reproducibility information. These administrative and formatting changes do not materially strengthen or weaken the paper's overall quality.
